name: OAuth redirect_uri validation bypass
description:
The authorization server validates redirect_uri weakly - by string prefix or by first value only - and redirected the flow to a manipulated spelling of the registered callback: an attacker subdomain of the registered host, a userinfo spelling, a traversal under the registered path, or a duplicate redirect_uri parameter whose second value was honoured. Each bypass delivers the victim's authorization code or access token to an attacker-controlled URI, which is one-click account takeover. The finding was proven by replaying the captured authorize request with manipulated redirect_uri values and reading the 302 Location the server produced.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's catalogue has no OAuth row; its open-redirection rows cover the generic primitive, but a redirect_uri bypass is an authorization failure, so this row rides 'Broken access control'.
remediation: Exact-match the full redirect_uri against the registered callbacks; reject duplicates and unregistered values outright - never prefix-, suffix- or substring-match. Where several callbacks are registered, match the whole string, not the origin.
